nodes.note: The cart road where it comes into Saltlow between two fence posts, with the whole street ahead and the quay at the far end of it.
Saltlow's one street: packed earth and cobbles, five wide, between low cottages, every door standing open the way people leave a house they do not mean to come back to.
The net-maker's cottage, first on the north side. Hooks on the walls where nets hung, a bare bench, a chest and a barrel that were emptied before the carts left.
The chandler's shop, on the south side. A counter with nothing on it, a barrel and a chest the chandler emptied into his cart.
The smokehouse, on the south side, its brick blackened. The smoker in the corner still holds the last fish of the last firing.

stations.note: The smoker itself, in the back corner of the smokehouse.

nodes.note: Marra Tarrow's cottage, last on the north side and nearest the quay. She went with the others, but left one chest at the foot of her bed with something in it for her brother.

stations.note: The chest at the foot of Marra's bed.

nodes.note: The stone quay at the east end of the street, where Ansel's ferry is tied up and waiting for the tide.

stations.note: Where Ansel stands, at the head of the quay steps, facing back up the street toward the road.
